analysis:
Every unit in this batch is a test file or a test build script. None of the changed code ships in the product.

PlacementSetupCheck.swift (lines 1260-1264): the `publicTrafficLine` assertions now pass `publicModels: []`. The check shows that with no public declaration, a pipeline family with no passing record stays "not yet qualified", and a family with a passing record reads "qualified for public traffic". Grants stay record-driven. This is a test of the public-grant logic for pair serving. It does not change the cache, attestation or coordinator boundaries.

run.sh (line 41): the test build now compiles `ClusterPublicModels.swift` into the placement check. The script only runs the local check and sets `-D DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_FIXTURE_ARTIFACTS`, which its own comment says never applies to a product build. I saw nothing that leaks the flag into production.

ClusterRuntimeFactsCommandTests.swift: adds parse coverage for the hidden `cluster runtime-facts` CLI modes `--list-release-models` and `--release-candidates`. It also adds rejection cases for mixed or incomplete flag combinations. The real parser and the file-reading code are not in this batch.

ClusterRuntimeApprovalFactsTests.swift: the metadata shows only a modified file, and I received no patch text or head text for it. I can therefore say nothing about its contents.

Open questions for later passes: first, how the new `--release-candidates` mode reads candidate files, and how it handles paths and trust. Second, how `ClusterPublicModels.swift` decides what counts as a public model, since it widens public-traffic qualification. Neither source file was supplied.

The cache threat T-041 appears in the supplied definitions, but nothing in this batch touches it. I found no security regression in the visible test changes.
